record.paper_title: Highlights and Open Questions from ZEUS
record.context_brief: Origin of forward D* photoproduction excess
record.original_question: In D* photoproduction at HERA, next-to-leading-order calculations typically underestimate the measured cross-section, and the excess appears predominantly in the forward direction. Is this discrepancy mainly caused by the choice of input photon structure function, by D* fragmentation dynamics as the measurement approaches the proton fragmentation region, or by anomalously large b -> c decay contributions?

evidence.quote: The measured cross-section is typically underestimated in the calculations. In Fig. 3(b) this excess is observed to be predominantly in the forward direction. The open question is whether the data are more sensitive to the choice of input photon structure function or to the D* fragmentation dynamics as we approach the proton fragmentation region or, perhaps, anomalously large contributions from b -> c decays.

artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent HERA measurements and NLO/FONLL/GM-VFNS analyses have reduced but not unambiguously eliminated the forward D* excess; improvements in the photon PDF (especially the gluon in the photon) and in charm fragmentation modeling both decrease the discrepancy, while b → c contributions are constrained to be small. A single, universally accepted attribution of the forward excess to one of the three listed causes has not been established in the literature accessed.

status_evidence.title: Dijet photoproduction at HERA and the structure of the photon
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of photon PDFs and forward-region sensitivity in HERA photoproduction.
status_evidence.claim: Photon structure (resolved-photon gluon) plays a role in forward photoproduction excesses but the gluon in the photon remains poorly constrained.

status_evidence.title: NLO photoproduction at HERA (DESY 10-088)
status_evidence.snippet: NLO calculations with phase-space regions where gluon-in-photon or gluon-in-proton dominate.
status_evidence.claim: NLO predictions for heavy-quark photoproduction have residual tensions with data sensitive to photon and proton gluon densities.
